summary: SEND-144 frontend verification on EST-176308 (338c6ac8-4e77-4dcd-84df-1cb7327b7ecb). BACKEND STATE IS CORRECT — API GET /photo-takeoff returns 23 marks across four AI-run photo_keys with all required basis text (AI front body basis contains '27.0 ft × 10.9 ft · width direct_ref · confidence 70 · starting position · NOT a measurement · 10.9 ft vs 9.0 ft · NOT averaged'; AI left body '37.0 ft × 8.4 ft'; AI left dormer 'UNANCHORED · no reference marker was in frame'; four AI opening marks on FRONT). FRONTEND INTEGRATION IS BROKEN — the AIMeasureButton 'PHOTO TAKEOFF' tile buttons open the editor keyed by the estimate's RAW UPLOADED photo_key (e.g. '603f3ba4b8c445c59d6767a41878baec.jpg' for the FRONT tile), while all AI zone marks live under the AI run's own photo_keys ('ai_f3c3b84ff88d467d91a8930064d0f737.jpg' for FRONT). Result: on every tile the editor shows 0 AI marks, the stage banner reads 'STAGE 1 — BEFORE AI', and the `photo-takeoff-zones-btn` renders DISABLED (the disabled attribute is present) because `stage?.stage !== 2` — so force-clicking it never fires the propose-zones request. The 'AI front body', 'AI front gable', four AI openings, 'AI left body', 'AI left dormer' and 'AI back body/gable' marks the reviewer asked us to see are unreachable through the current UI entry point. NOTHING WAS DELETED, CONFIRMED, APPLIED, OR RE-SCALED. Zones remain in place as instructed.

integration_issues.flow: SEND-144 handoff — Photo Takeoff editor on the FRONT/LEFT/BACK tiles cannot see the AI zone marks
integration_issues.issue: The `ai-measure-photo-takeoff-<i>` button in AIMeasureButton.jsx (line 3468) calls setTakeoffOpenFor(name) where `name` is the estimate's uploaded photo filename ('603f3ba4b8c445c59d6767a41878baec.jpg' for tile 0). The AI-run photos, however, live under different photo_keys prefixed 'ai_' (e.g. 'ai_f3c3b84ff88d467d91a8930064d0f737.jpg' is the FRONT face). face_for_photo() and build_zone_marks() correctly stored the SEND-144 zones under those `ai_*` keys, so a GET /photo-takeoff?photo_key=ai_f3c3b84ff88d467d91a8930064d0f737.jpg returns all six FRONT AI marks with the expected basis text, BUT the frontend never opens the editor with that key. As a consequence on every uploaded tile: (a) marks list is empty — no 'AI front body', no 'AI front gable', no AI openings; (b) stage_banner shows STAGE 1 and disables `photo-takeoff-zones-btn`; (c) `photo-takeoff-proposals-refusal` reads the generic 'no completed AI read carries this photo — Stage 2 is not unlocked here' instead of the SEND-144 face-specific refusals (RIGHT's assumed_symmetric refusal, or the corner-shot refusal); (d) no <CandidateEdges> render because there is no body siding_zone on the tile's photo_key. Even the RESTORE PREVIEW view (which shows all 8 `ai_*` images in its preview strip) does not expose a takeoff entry point onto those ai_-keyed photos.

action_items: The 'PHOTO TAKEOFF' entry point (AIMeasureButton.jsx line 3466-3475) must open PhotoTakeoffEditor keyed to the AI-run photo when one exists for that tile. Either (a) map each uploaded tile's photo to its AI-annotated counterpart via ai_measure_runs.photos[i].photo_key (or elevation match) and pass that key to setTakeoffOpenFor(...); or (b) add a separate takeoff entry point on the RESTORE PREVIEW pane so each `ai_*.jpg` image has its own 'Photo Takeoff' button carrying the ai_* photo_key. Without one of these, SEND-144 is invisible to a contractor.

Once the editor is opened on the AI-run photo_key, re-verify: (1) 'AI front body' row + expanded basis carries the seven substrings ['27.0 ft × 10.9 ft', 'width direct_ref', 'confidence 70', 'starting position', 'not a measurement', '10.9 ft vs 9.0 ft', 'NOT averaged']; (2) `photo-takeoff-candidate-edges-<markId>` renders with labels 'starter candidate', 'corner candidate' (×2), 'eave / frieze candidate' AND NO NUMERIC TEXT; (3) `photo-takeoff-zones-btn` is enabled and the second press keeps the mark count identical (idempotency toast '…starting zones are already here; nothing was overwritten'); (4) RIGHT elevation editor surfaces the SEND-144 assumed_symmetric refusal and creates no marks; (5) any corner-shot editor surfaces the 'corner shot is NOT a fifth wall … foreshortened' refusal and creates no marks; (6) LEFT editor shows 'AI left body' (37.0 ft × 8.4 ft) + 'AI left dormer' (UNANCHORED · no reference marker in frame).
critical_code_review_comments: AIMeasureButton.jsx uses `setTakeoffOpenFor(name)` where `name` is the uploaded photo filename. It does not consult ai_measure_runs.photos[i].photo_key, so any run that stores its own `ai_*` versions of the photos silently strands the AI-produced marks. This is not a data problem — the backend photo_zone_proposals code correctly persisted the zones under the AI photo_keys and the routes correctly return them; the frontend simply never asks for that key.

PhotoTakeoffEditor.jsx pullZones() (line 237) is unreachable when stage !== 2. force-clicking a disabled button (from playwright or a real user) is a no-op. Recommend also surfacing the reason on the disabled button's tooltip (already present via `stage.proposals_refusal`) and, more importantly, wiring the correct photo_key so the button un-disables on the AI-run tiles.

CandidateEdges.jsx is correct: labels are pure words ('starter candidate', 'corner candidate' (×2), 'eave / frieze candidate') with no length/LF/number token in the SVG <text> body. When a body siding_zone finally reaches the editor this component will render as expected — no fix needed there.
photo_zone_proposals.face_for_photo() logic is sound (verified via the API refusal messages that WILL be shown once the editor sees the ai_* key).

context_for_next_testing_agent: The eight items in the review request are all verifiable AT THE API LEVEL (GET /api/estimates/338c6ac8-4e77-4dcd-84df-1cb7327b7ecb/photo-takeoff?photo_key=<ai_key>) and every basis/refusal string is verbatim correct in the DB — see verification_evidence above. What is missing is a UI ROUTE that opens the takeoff editor keyed to `ai_<hash>.jpg`. Once E1 wires that route, re-run tests 1,2,4,5 on the FRONT AI photo, test 6 on the RIGHT face (should refuse), test 7 on any front-left/rear-left/rear-right/front-right corner photo (should refuse), and test 8 on the LEFT AI photo. The zones ARE PLACED and MUST BE LEFT IN PLACE per Howard's rule — do not delete/confirm/apply. Watch data-testid `photo-takeoff-candidate-edges-<markId>` for a regression toward numeric labels.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE — the AI Measure run creates its own set of processed photos (`ai_<hash>.jpg`) and photo_zone_proposals.build_zone_marks correctly stamps the SEND-144 zone marks with those `ai_*` photo_keys (photo_zone_proposals.py line 215: `"photo_key": photo_key` where photo_key comes from `_run_photo_names(run)`). The frontend, however, still opens PhotoTakeoffEditor on the estimate's ORIGINAL uploaded photo (AIMeasureButton.jsx line 3468 `setTakeoffOpenFor(name)` where `name` is the uploaded filename from Adjust-Photos, e.g. `603f3ba4b8c445c59d6767a41878baec.jpg`). Since the two keys differ, GET /photo-takeoff?photo_key=<uploaded> returns marks: [] for the AI zones and per_photo[<uploaded>].stage=1 (no AI read against this key), which disables the zones button and shows the generic 'no completed AI read carries this photo' refusal instead of any SEND-144 refusal. REPRODUCTION: login → /estimate/338c6ac8-… → AI MEASURE → resume → ADJUST PHOTOS → click PHOTO TAKEOFF under the FRONT tile → observe marks_count=0, stage='STAGE 1 — BEFORE AI', starting-zones button disabled. Compare with GET /api/estimates/338c6ac8-.../photo-takeoff?photo_key=ai_f3c3b84ff88d467d91a8930064d0f737.jpg → 6 marks returned including AI front body/gable and 4 openings. MITIGATION: in AIMeasureButton.jsx, when a completed run exists for the estimate, resolve each tile's AI photo_key from ai_measure_runs.result.photos[<tile-elevation>] (or by matching tile index → run photo index) and pass that key (not the raw upload name) into setTakeoffOpenFor(). Alternatively add a dedicated 'Photo Takeoff' button on each thumbnail in the RESTORE PREVIEW pane, bound to the ai_* key. Either fix unblocks SEND-144 end-to-end.
